story.head: The Bruins’ edge in shot quality
paras: The Bruins won the teams’ first meeting this season, 4-3 in overtime in Winnipeg on Oct 2. The Bruins have won two in a row, and the Jets (12-9-4) beat Utah 4-2 on Monday. Going in, the Jets are sixth in the Central (tied for 14th in the NHL) and the Bruins fourth in the Atlantic (tenth).

The Jets’ record (.560) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.499), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games. So is the Bruins’ (.674 on chances worth .576), largely thanks to their goaltending.

The Jets create more chances on the penalty kill than almost anyone (3rd) and rarely ice the puck (4th). They also get their shots through better than almost anyone (3rd), and their knack for getting shots through meets the Bruins’ shot blockers. The Bruins leave the shooting to their forwards (lowest), sit back rather than chase on the forecheck (2nd lowest) and have had some of the league’s best goaltending (3rd). Boston has allowed 2.65 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league. The Bruins have the edge over the Jets on shot quality.

Kyle Connor (19 G / 13 A / 32 P in 25 GP) leads the Jets in scoring and is tied for ninth in the NHL, with eight points in his last five games. Mark Scheifele (8 G / 23 A / 31 P in 25 GP) is next in line, with nine points in his last five games and four goals in six games against Boston since 2023-24. The Bruins’ scoring runs through David Pastrňák (11 G / 20 A / 31 P in 23 GP), who has seven points in his last five games and a point in six straight games against Winnipeg. Elias Lindholm (11 G / 11 A / 22 P in 23 GP) isn’t far behind, with seven points in his last five games.
Nico Daws (5-3-0 / .891 SV% in 7 GS) is expected to start for Winnipeg, and Jeremy Swayman (11-5-1 / .904 SV% in 17 GS) for Boston.
